title: Justin Kadi
text:
I’m Justin Kadi, an environmental data scientist working at the National Center for Ecological Analysis and Synthesis (NCEAS) at UC Santa Barbara as a Projects Data Coordinator. I work with NSF’s Arctic Data Center (ADC), where I curate and publish 340+ TB of Arctic research data, and on the Permafrost Discovery Gateway (PDG), where I process and visualize pan-Arctic permafrost datasets.
I’m broadly interested in the intersection of data science with environmental and climate science. Currently, I’m learning more about geospatial data processing and its use cases in environmental projects.
Before coming to NCEAS, I researched physics-informed deep learning models for streamflow forecasting at UC Berkeley, built short-term weather forecast ensembles at ClimateAi, and developed a semantic search system for mission documents at NASA Ames. All these experiences contributed to my excitement for the potential impacts of data and computational methods in our understanding of our planet.

title: Pan-Arctic Permafrost Visualization
text: The Permafrost Discovery Gateway (PDG) is an online platform for creating, analyzing, and visualizing big geospatial permafrost products to enable knowledge generation about the changing Arctic landscape. It gives researchers, educators, and the public access to very high resolution, satellite-derived data products across the Arctic.

title: Pan-Arctic Permafrost Visualization
text:
My Role
I work with researchers to process their datasets through the PDG visualization pipeline: staging, tiling, and rasterizing large vector and raster datasets so they can be explored in the data portal. Many of these datasets are pan-Arctic products derived from machine learning models applied to satellite imagery.

Run automated, parallelized tiling workflows on UCSB’s high-performance computing clusters
Contribute to open-source tooling for Cesium 3D tiling

title: Semantic Search for NASA Mission Documents
text:
NASA missions produce thousands of requirements documents, reports, and artifacts that reviewers must search through for evidence. In the Intelligent Systems Division at NASA Ames, working with Nija Shi and Guillaume Brat, I developed a semantic search and question answering system, built into a project management dashboard, to speed up this auditing process.



How the system works: project documents are processed through an ETL pipeline and fine-tuned BERT models into an Elasticsearch index, which powers a search and question answering dashboard for mission reviewers.

title: Semantic Search for NASA Mission Documents
text:
My Role

Built a semantic search system, used on 3 missions, that analyzes 2,000+ project documents and retrieves critical evidence for reviews
Fine-tuned BERT transformer language models to better represent NASA-specific phrases & acronyms, improving correct retrieval by 30+%
Added a question answering tool to the dashboard, expediting document auditing by 3+ months
Designed ETL and search pipelines with Elasticsearch, connected to a NodeJS/React front end through the Haystack REST API

title: Physics-Informed LSTMs for Streamflow
text: Deep learning models such as Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks can forecast streamflow well, but they are often treated as black boxes. In Laurel Larsen’s Environmental Systems Dynamics Lab at UC Berkeley, we explored whether building physics-based constraints into an LSTM improves its forecasts, and whether the model’s internal structure reconstructs physical processes in the watershed.

title: Physics-Informed LSTMs for Streamflow
text: Deep learning models such as Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks can forecast streamflow well, but they are often treated as black boxes. In Laurel Larsen’s Environmental Systems Dynamics Lab at UC Berkeley, we explored whether building physics-based constraints into an LSTM improves its forecasts, and whether the model’s internal structure reconstructs physical processes in the watershed.

title: Physics-Informed LSTMs for Streamflow
text:
My Role

Designed LSTM neural networks in PyTorch to forecast watershed discharge from temperature & precipitation time series
Added physics-based constraints to the model structure, improving accuracy by 5%
Implemented time series cross-validation to test robustness across 30 datasets in varying climates
Built Python visualization scripts to compare and analyze 2+ million graphs, supporting the hypothesis that a network’s internal structure can reconstruct physical processes

title: Meta-Model Weather Forecasting
text: No single weather forecast is best everywhere. At ClimateAi, I built a meta-model that combines several public and private forecasts, weighting each one by its recent skill at each location and lead time, to produce more accurate short-term forecasts of mean temperature and precipitation.

title: Meta-Model Weather Forecasting
text: No single weather forecast is best everywhere. At ClimateAi, I built a meta-model that combines several public and private forecasts, weighting each one by its recent skill at each location and lead time, to produce more accurate short-term forecasts of mean temperature and precipitation.

title: Meta-Model Weather Forecasting
text:
My Role

Designed a multi-model ensemble algorithm combining 6 data sources, with separate weights for 30 customer locations and 4 lead times
Improved short-term forecasts by 20% over the best vendor’s model
Built automated Google Cloud pipelines for geospatial data extraction, preprocessing, and forecast skill & uncertainty analysis, updating the model weights weekly
Presented Tableau map visualizations comparing our model’s performance with competitors’
